items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to the granting of tenure
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5576

SPONSOR: MAYER
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law, in relation to the granting of tenure

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This bill would provide a tenure process for probationary teachers,
principals, and supervising staff aligned with changes necessary under
the Covid-19 pandemic in regard to annual professional performance
reviews (APPRs) for the 2020-21 school year.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Sections 1, 3, 4, and 5 of the bill amend various provisions of educa-
tion law pertaining to the granting of tenure by allowing teachers,
principals, or other supervising staff, who were appointed in the 2017-
18, 2018-19 or 2019-20 school years to be eligible for tenure if they
had received either an effective or highly effected composite APPR
rating in at least one of the last four years.  Additionally, under the
bill these individuals would not be eligible for tenure if they received
an ineffective rating in the final year of their probationary period or
the most recent year that a rating was given. These sections also
provide tenured teachers, principals and supervising staff who accepted
a position in another school district in 2020-21 to be appointed for the
probationary period of three years provided they received an APPR rating
in either the 2017-18 or 201819 school years.

Section 2 of the bill waives school districts' responsibility to conduct
the APPR process for the 2020-21 school year and ensures that state
funding is not withheld accordingly.

Section 6 establishes the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Last year, school closures under the Covid-19 pandemic necessitated a
waiver in regard to state assessments and subsequently the annual
professional performance review of teachers, principals and other super-
vising staff. Absent an APPR in 2019-20, individuals in probationary
status were eligible to be granted tenure based on their APPR ratings of
prior applicable years.

Unfortunately, this year Covid-19 has continued to present a challenge
for school openings and there are inconsistencies across the State,
regions and within districts about the delivery of in-person instruc-
tion. While schools continue to advance full reopening plans, many
students continue to be on hybrid or full remote learning schedules.
Additionally, the recent decision by the United States Department of
Education to require states to administer standardized testing, does not
support the request of the New York State Education Department to waive
state assessments and subsequently the APPR process for this year.
Accountability measurements from required state assessments for this
year should not be considered for purposes of evaluating professional
performance.


This legislation will continue to recognize the impact Covid-19 has had
on students, teachers and administrators by excluding state assessments
from being used to measure professional performance this year and
continue to authorize the granting of tenure.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 8  Chapter 112
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 5576-C, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to amend the education law, in relation to the granting of
        tenure"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This legislation would suspend the requirement for schools to  perform
teacher  and  principal  performance  evaluations for the 2020-21 school
year and modify corresponding requirements to achieve  tenure  based  on
those evaluations.
 
  On  June  7,  2020,  at  the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, I issued
Executive Order 202.39, which suspended the use of  Annual  Professional
Performance Review (APPR) evaluations for teachers and principals in New
York's  schools.  In  weighing the fairness to teachers of performing an
evaluation during an ongoing crisis situation, EO  202.39  also  allowed
teachers  and  principals  to be granted tenure even though they had not
received an APPR rating, as long as their superintendent  attested  that
their performance qualified them for tenure.
 
  Throughout  this pandemic, our teachers and school administrators have
continued to triage, innovate, and above all educate, despite  extremely
difficult  circumstances.  I  applaud  the  Legislature  in passing this
legislation, which continues to recognize the impact of the pandemic  on
our  teachers  and  principals, and allows for a clear path to attaining
tenure.
 
  In order to ensure that our  schools  have  consistency  and  a  clear
understanding  of  what  the  suspension  of APPR and granting of tenure
require, I have secured an agreement with the Legislature to pass legis-
lation bringing the requirements of the current bill into alignment with
last year's Executive Order 202.39,  including  flexibility  for  school
districts  in  suspending  APPR  requirements as well as defining tenure
qualification for those impacted by the suspension of APPR. On the basis
of this agreement, I am signing this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                      (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                                ______

summary: Relates to the granting of tenure to probationary classroom teachers or building principals; provides that no school district shall complete an annual professional performance review for the two thousand twenty--two thousand twenty-one school year.
